svg.title: For joint two-point tests use their relative wave transform. The normalized position dilation fρ(x) = ρdf(ρx) satisfies bfρ,+(p) = bf+(p/ρ) by change of variables. The same identity for the joint wave transform carries (TR9) to the source’s relative and joint Wightman distribution limits. We now prove the polynomial growth and Laplace continuity assertions used in (TR6)–(TR9), then the finite mass-shell obstruction. The subsequent stress correction and Ward calculation derive the trace coefficient and its Wilson normalization.
